context: Ibrahim is Makkan and was sent down to the people of a city Ibrahim had asked Allah to make secure, whose sanctuary and water they still lived off. They traced their descent to him, kept the pilgrimage he had established, and had filled the House he built with idols. Some early authorities read two of its verses as pointing to the Quraysh who fell at Badr, and that reading is disputed.

What follows is built out of speech: a Book sent down to bring people from the darknesses into the light, every messenger sent in the tongue of his own people, a good word compared to a rooted tree, and at the end Ibrahim speaking for seven verses. The founder of the city asks for exactly what his descendants had abandoned. He asks to be kept away from idols, and the people hearing this were standing among them.
name_story: Ibrahim does not appear until verse 35, and when he arrives he neither argues with anyone nor breaks anything. He prays. Naming a surah after a passage of supplication rather than a story is unusual, and it points a reader at the fact that the man who built the sanctuary spent his prayer worrying about idolatry among his own descendants.

movements.h: Out of the darknesses into the light
movements.note: The purpose of the revelation is stated in the first verse and repeated for Musa in the fifth, with the order to remind his people of the days of Allah. Verse 7 sets out the rule of increase for gratitude.

movements.h: The record of the earlier peoples
movements.note: Nuh, 'Ad and Thamud are named without their stories, and the exchange is reduced to essentials: a demand for proof, a threat of expulsion, a promise of the land to those who remain.

movements.h: Shaytan's speech, and the two trees
movements.note: Once judgement is passed, Shaytan denies holding any authority over his followers beyond an invitation they accepted. Then the good word as a tree with fixed roots and branches in the sky, and the corrupt word as a tree pulled up from the surface.

movements.h: The favours that cannot be counted
movements.note: Ships running at His command, rivers, the sun and moon in constant service, night and day, and the statement that the favours of Allah cannot be counted by anyone who tries.
Ibrahim asks for security for the city, for protection from idols, for hearts to incline toward the family left in a bare valley, and for prayer to be kept up by him and his descendants.
A warning against supposing Allah unaware of what wrongdoers do, the earth replaced by another earth, and a last verse describing the surah itself as a notification.

themes.t: Revelation as speech in a known tongue
themes.d: Every messenger was sent in the language of his people, given at verse 4 as a condition of making things clear. The surah keeps returning to words: the word that roots, the word that is torn up, the invitation Shaytan admits was only ever an invitation.
Verse 7 does not praise gratitude as a virtue but states it as a cause with an announced effect, naming the alternative in the same breath.
Shaytan's speech at verse 22 is a disclaimer after the fact: he called, they answered, and he asks them not to blame him.
Ibrahim asks to be kept from idols after a lifetime of breaking them, and asks the same for his sons, in front of an audience descended from him who had done exactly what he feared.

heart: Ibrahim is a short surah with an unusually steady voice. Nothing in it is narrated at length, and slow recitation works by accumulation rather than drama: light and darkness, a rooted tree and an uprooted one, favours beyond counting, a day on which eyes do not blink.

The part most readers carry is the supplication, which repays being read whole, because it moves outward in a definite order: the city, then protection from idols for himself and his sons, then the descendants left in the bare valley, then his parents, then all the believers. One verse of it, the line where Ibrahim says that whoever follows him is of him, was recited by the Prophet ﷺ before he raised his hands and wept for his community.

passages.why: If you are grateful, I will increase you. A condition stated plainly, with the consequence of the opposite named immediately after.
Shaytan's address to his followers once judgement is over, admitting he had no authority except that he called and they answered.
The good word as a good tree, its root fixed and its branches in the sky, giving fruit every season by the permission of its Lord.
Ibrahim asking to be made someone who keeps up the prayer, then asking forgiveness for his parents and the believers on the day of reckoning. The words are ancient and are still said.

connections.why: Al-Baqarah gives the same supplication at the House from another angle at verses 126 to 129.
Al-An'am shows Ibrahim reasoning his way to the One God as a young man. This surah shows him much later, asking that the conclusion hold in his children.

virtue.text: No authentic report establishes a specific merit for reciting Surah Ibrahim. What is authentically recorded involves one of its verses rather than the surah: the Prophet ﷺ recited the words of Ibrahim at verse 36, then raised his hands, asked twice for his community and wept, in Muslim 202. That report says nothing about a reward for reciting, and the surah's standing rests on the supplication at verses 35 to 41.
virtue.src: no virtue-of-recitation report; the Prophet ﷺ reciting 14:36 and weeping for his community, Muslim 202
